plan.summary: BRO-7245: add a commercial entry for Legally Blonde (2007, Palace Theatre), which had none.
steps: Capitalization $12.8M from lead producer Hal Luftig in Wealth Manager (Sept 2006): 'With Blonde, my total budget is $12.8 million'.
Did not recoup on Broadway: Daily Herald (May 6, 2009): 'The show closed in October 2008, failing to fully recoup its original investment of $13 million.'

No source reports how much of the capitalization came back, so the label is Did Not Recoup. The '75% returned by closing' claim traces only to a Jan 2008 BroadwayWorld forum projection and the $600-650K weekly nut is forum-only; neither is used.

entry.recoupedSource: Daily Herald (May 6, 2009): "The show closed in October 2008, failing to fully recoup its original investment of $13 million." https://www.dailyherald.com/20090506/lifestyle/creative-marketing-saved-chicago-bound-legally-blonde/
entry.capitalizationSource: Wealth Manager (Sep 1, 2006), lead producer Hal Luftig: "With 'Blonde,' my total budget is $12.8 million." https://jrliebermancpa.com/wp-content/uploads/2011/07/BROADWAY-BUSINESS-WEALTH-MANAGER-2006.pdf
entry.notes: Commercial musical at the Palace Theatre (opened Apr 29, 2007; closed Oct 19, 2008 after 595 performances). Lead producer Hal Luftig put the total budget at $12.8M, including about $1.5M for a San Francisco tryout. Grossed about $56M on Broadway and closed without recouping, after grosses fell in fall 2008. No published source says how much of the capitalization came back; a '75% by closing' figure that circulates online traces only to a January 2008 forum projection. The national tour, the West End production and licensing pay royalties to the Broadway company, but no source reports the investors being made whole.

actions.description: legally-blonde-2007: add commercial entry (Did Not Recoup, $12.8M capitalization)
